evidence.quote: let renewalRefusal (today: DateOnly) (loan: Loan) (library: Library) : RenewalRefusal option =
match renewalRefusal today loan library with
match renewalRefusal today loan library with
NotRenewable = Loans.renewalRefusal today loan library |> Option.map describeRefusal

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The renewability rule and the order of its reasons (overdue, limit reached, holds) are decided once, in Tier 2's Loans.renewalRefusal. Loans.renew, Loans.renewAll (also Tier 2) and the Tier 3 projection Views.ofLoan all call that one function. Tier 3 only maps the closed RenewalRefusal type to display text (describeRefusal) and counts renewed entries. The CLI only renders the view's Option and makes no decision of its own.

evidence.quote: | Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effect below Tier 4. Today's date comes in through the Clock port, and state is loaded and saved through the existing commit/query helpers over the Store port. Tier 1/2 code stays pure: it takes `today` and a Library and returns values. The change also removes an existing violation in which the CLI loaded the Store, called Loans.renew in Tier 2 directly and saved (removed lines 180-186). That path now goes through the Tier 3 use case.

evidence.quote: elif loan.Renewals >= Policy.renewLimit then Some(RenewalsUsed(loan.Renewals, Policy.renewLimit))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Every use of the renewal limit and the loan period refers to the single Policy definition, and no literal is copied into production code. The refusal reasons are defined once in the RenewalRefusal type and turned into text in one place (describeRefusal), which both the loans and renew-all outputs use.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new rule (the limit is the borrower's, by member type) is decided in Tier 2: Policy.renewLimit maps member type to a number, and Loans.renewalLimit looks up the borrower. renewalRefusal uses it for the guard. Tier 3's projection calls Loans.renewalLimit to show the limit and does not re-derive it.

evidence.quote: |> Result.map (fun (l, loan) -> l, Views.ofRenew l loan))

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no new effect. renewalLimit is a pure lookup on the Library value, and the use cases still reach the store and clock only through the existing ports. Nothing in Tier 4 changed.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The limits for each member type are defined once, in Policy.renewLimit, and the borrower lookup once, in Loans.renewalLimit. The guard, the refusal reason and the renew view all use that function, so the old single limit and the new per-type limits cannot both be in force. The refusal error carries the limit from the same value.
